issues.translation_quote: That's not topical! "The Island of Bad Luck"!
issues.justification: 'Not topical' is unnatural in English and misses the comic register. The point is 'that's not the thing' / 'that's not in fashion' / 'that's not relevant now.' The joke's timing suffers from the stiff phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: Russo Turisto! Obliko Morale! Verstehen? Russo Turisto... Obliko Morale... Verstehen?
issues.justification: The phrase is iconic mock-macaronic comedy. Repeating it twice in the subtitles where the source only presents it once as the punch dulls the joke, and leaving it entirely untranslated gives no help to viewers unfamiliar with the film. Some support like 'Soviet tourist—moral character, understand?' would preserve the humor and meaning.

issues.translation_quote: Passed out. Woke up in a cast.
issues.justification: This catchphrase is central and recurs throughout the film. 'Woke up in a cast' is understandable, but it loses the abrupt clipped comic rhythm of 'came to — cast!' A sharper recurring English hook was needed for consistency and humor.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: As our dear boss says, in our line of work the main thing is realism!
issues.justification: The source has comic criminal pomposity plus malapropistic flavor. The translation is semantically correct but too plain, missing the pompous mock-professional tone that makes the line funny.

issues.source_quote: Товарищ, товарищ, товарищ, хорошо бы ай-лю-лю, цигель, цигель - время, товарищ!
issues.translation_quote: Comrade, comrade, comrade, it'd be good to— ai-lyu-lyu, zigel, zigel—time, comrade!
issues.justification: This is a famous line and a comic high point. The translation is nearly uninterpretable English, so the punchline fails. The meaning is roughly 'Less ai-lyu-lyu, more zigel-zigel — time's up!' and needs an idiomatic comic solution.

issues.source_quote: Если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: If a man is an idiot, it's for a long time!
issues.justification: The literal wording is intelligible, but the recurring punchline needs an idiomatic, quotable form. 'If someone's an idiot, that's a life sentence' or similar would better carry the comic sting. As translated, it sounds clunky and repeatedly lessens one of the film's signature lines.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты жил на одну зарплату!
issues.translation_quote: May you live... on nothing but... your salary!
issues.justification: This iconic curse is culturally loaded and comic precisely because it sounds absurdly petty in Soviet conditions. The literal rendering communicates denotation but not the force or humor. It needs a more pointed equivalent or at least sharper phrasing to land.
This captures vulgarity, but 'broad' sounds American and period-marked in a way that may not suit the overall register. A less regionally marked colloquial insult might fit better.

issues.translation_quote: With a light flick of the wrist, the trousers transform... The trousers transform... Transform, the trousers do... into elegant shorts.
issues.justification: The phrase is famous for its escalating comic repetition and the suit/pants mishap. The Yoda-like 'Transform, the trousers do' is a serious misfire and sounds unintentionally bizarre rather than theatrically comic.
The Russian word is left in Cyrillic inside an English sentence. This is untranslated material in a key comedic exchange and clearly a translation failure.

issues.source_quote: Ребята, на его месте должен быть я. Напьёшься - будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Guys, I should have been in his place! — Get drunk enough, and you will be!
issues.justification: The line is understandable, but 'get drunk enough, and you will be' is stiff. A snappier comeback would better preserve the joke's rhythm.

issues.source_quote: Наши люди в булочную на такси не ездят!
issues.translation_quote: Our people don't take taxis to the bakery!
issues.justification: This iconic line is translated literally, but without context it sounds merely odd. It needs a more pointed colloquial rendering to preserve its aphoristic comic force in English.

issues.source_quote: Кто возьмёт билетов пачку, тот получит... Водокачку!
issues.translation_quote: Buy a whole ticket pack, win... a tractor rack!
issues.justification: The source is a rhyme-joke and slogan parody. 'Tractor rack' is semantically off and not funny. The wordplay fails to cross into English, which is a major style loss under the instructions.

issues.source_quote: Будете у нас на Колыме - милости просим! Нет уж, лучше вы к нам!
issues.translation_quote: Well, if you're ever in Kolyma... — No, better you visit us!
issues.justification: The dark joke hinges on Kolyma's connotations and the deadpan response. The translation is literal but fails to help the target viewer grasp why it's funny; the cultural joke largely falls flat.

issues.source_quote: Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!
issues.translation_quote: In the morning, champagne is drunk only by aristocrats and degenerates.
issues.justification: The wording is stiff and unquotable. This famous line needs a sharper, idiomatic form to preserve its punch and comic contrast.
The source jokes with a foreign accent, but the transcription trick in English is opaque and unnatural. It neither translates the meaning elegantly nor recreates the joke effectively.

issues.source_quote: Не виноватая я! Он сам пришёл!
issues.translation_quote: Twasn't my fault! He came here on his own!
issues.justification: The line is intelligible, but 'Twasn't' gives it an archaic or dialect flavor not present in the original. A more natural colloquial English line would better suit the melodramatic parody.
